US Tariffs Hit Denmark’s Transportation Equipment Sector, Prompting Layoffs and Production Slowdowns

Danish transportation equipment manufacturers are facing mounting pressure after the United States imposed a 25% tariff on imports of Danish-made rail vehicles, marine equipment, and cargo handling machinery earlier this month. The measure, announced without prior warning, is already reverberating across the industry’s production sites and workforce.

Several Danish firms, including Nordisk TransTech and Skagen Equipment Works, report that shipments to the US have been delayed or cancelled outright. “We rely on the US market for nearly 30% of our annual sales,” said Lone Madsen, CEO of Nordisk TransTech. “With these tariffs, our products are suddenly far less competitive, and buyers are already postponing orders.”

Industry association Dansk Transportudstyrforening estimates that sector exports to the US were worth DKK 2.1 billion last year. Now, factories in Odense and Esbjerg are reducing shifts and implementing temporary layoffs. “We have had to send 40 workers home this week,” confirmed Henrik Juul, operations manager at Skagen Equipment Works’ Esbjerg site. “If the situation continues, more jobs will be at risk.”

According to analyst Peter Holst, “The immediate impact is being felt on assembly lines and shop floors. Companies are scaling back production volumes due to the sudden drop in demand.” Sector unions have called for urgent government support, warning of further job losses if the tariffs remain in place.

The government is reportedly in talks with US officials, but with the trade measure still in effect, the Danish transportation equipment industry is bracing for continued challenges in the months ahead.
